issues.legal_issue: An application to reject a plaint for failure to disclose a cause of action or because the suit is barred by law must be decided from the plaint’s allegations, without awaiting the defendant’s written statement.
material_facts: A defendant applied to have the plaint rejected, asserting that it disclosed no cause of action and that the suit was barred by law.
The trial court directed the defendant to file a written statement without first deciding the rejection application.
The High Court upheld that direction and instructed the trial court to frame and decide preliminary issues.
issues.conclusion: The rejection application had to be decided on the plaint’s allegations, and the defendant’s written statement was irrelevant to that decision. Requiring the written statement without deciding the application was a procedural irregularity and a failure to exercise jurisdiction. The challenged order was set aside, and the cases were remitted for the trial court to decide the application after hearing the parties.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the relevant material for deciding whether a plaint discloses a cause of action or appears barred by law is the plaint’s averments; the defendant’s written statement is wholly irrelevant at that stage. The court may exercise this power at any stage before conclusion of the trial. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.plaint_rejection_application_pending: A party to a civil suit has applied for rejection of the plaint.
predicates.application_alleges_no_cause_or_legal_ba: The application asserts that the plaint discloses no cause of action or that the suit is barred by law.

issues.definition: When a party seeks rejection of a plaint on the stated grounds, the court decides that application from the plaint before requiring a written statement.
